title: Spire Codex - Ultimate Companion & Stats Aggregator
description:
[h1]Spire Codex - Ultimate Companion & Stats Aggregator[/h1]
Spire Codex brings the power of spire-codex.com directly into Slay the Spire 2. No more alt-tabbing to check stats mid-run.

Whether you're new to the climb or grinding Ascension 10, Spire Codex gives you data-driven insight (Codex Elo + Codex Score) at a glance to help you make winning decisions. When your run ends it's automatically saved to https://spire-codex.com.

[h2]Features[/h2]
- Automatic run tracking: Every run uploads and competes on the leaderboards, and gets its own shareable page on the website.
- In-game community tooltips: Win rates and Codex tiers shown natively on the game's own tooltips for cards, relics, potions, events, and campfire options.
- Stat brackets: Filter the community numbers by bracket (All runs, Ascension 10, or higher win-rate players) so you can follow what competitive players actually pick.
- Live damage meter: Track your damage per turn, total, biggest hit, and damage taken in combat. Drag it anywhere on screen.
- Personal insights: Your own pick rates and run history shown alongside the community stats.
- Map route & danger: A recommended route plus per-node danger ratings from community data (Codex Risk).
- Import vanilla saves: Modded Slay the Spire 2 keeps its own separate save folder, so your unlocks and run history look empty after you install mods. Copy an unmodded profile across from a button on the profile select screen, or from the Import tab in the overlay. Based on Ind-E's ImportVanillaSaves mod (https://github.com/Ind-E/ImportVanillaSaves), used with permission.
- In-overlay settings: Toggle every on-screen surface and pick your stat bracket right from the F5 panel.
- Localized in 15 languages: The whole mod follows your game's language automatically, including card, relic, potion, monster, and character names.

[h2]Controls[/h2]
- Open/close the overlay: F5 (or click either stick, R3/L3, on a controller)
- Switch tabs: Tab (or L1/R1 / LB/RB on a controller)
- Open the settings from the main menu: Spire Codex Settings

[h2]References[/h2]
Find out more about Spire Codex through our GitHub, Overwolf, and the main website.

[h2]Credits[/h2]
Save importing is based on ImportVanillaSaves by Ind-E (https://github.com/Ind-E/ImportVanillaSaves), used with permission.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
Requires BaseLib
changeNote:
Spire Codex can now bring your vanilla saves over to your modded profile.

Modded Slay the Spire 2 saves to its own folder, so the first time you launch with mods your unlocks and run history look like they're gone. They aren't, they're just in the unmodded folder. There's now an Import button on the profile select screen, and a matching Import tab in the overlay, that copies a vanilla profile across for you. Copying the folder by hand doesn't stick, because the game's cloud sync deletes the files again on the next launch, so this writes through the game's own save system instead. Thanks to Ind-E and the ImportVanillaSaves mod (https://github.com/Ind-E/ImportVanillaSaves) for working out how this has to be done, and for letting me build on it.

Also in this update:
- Spire Codex Settings is now on the main menu, instead of being buried in Mod Configuration.
- New Backfill past runs button in the settings, with progress. You can upload your run history whenever you want now, not just on first launch. Runs already on the site get skipped, and uploads pace themselves so they don't hit the rate limit.
- The overlay now uses the game's own Kreon font and one consistent gold, so it sits better alongside the game's UI.
- Added Traditional Chinese. The mod is now in all 15 of the game's languages.
- Fixed controller stick click, which stopped working when the game renamed that input in v0.109.1. It was also filling the log with errors.
- Removed the Current Run tab. Live run info lives in the Overwolf overlay.
